title: Full stack software, end to end
description: I like owning a feature the whole way, from the data model to the screen, and shaping it with the people who'll use it. The best part is when an interface makes a complicated system feel obvious.

title: Software that has to be right
description: I'm drawn to software where a mistake is costly and quiet, like money moving or records people rely on. I like designing it so that wrong answers are hard to produce, with clear invariants, idempotent operations and tests that fail the build.

title: Data in motion
description: I like what happens to data after it leaves the system it was born in, and the edge cases that change the design, such as ordering, replays, schema changes and deletes. A snapshot cannot see a record that is gone.

title: Automating the tedious
description: I like finding a manual, repetitive process and turning it into something that runs by itself, safely, whether that is a deployment, a provisioning request or a nightly job. The best version is the one nobody has to think about.

title: Life after launch
description: Shipping is the middle of the story. I like the work that comes after, reading a system under stress, chasing the real cause instead of the symptom, and leaving runbooks and mentoring so the next engineer can carry it.

title: Language models that earn their place
description: When something breaks overnight, someone has to work out what happened. I want to see where a language model earns its place in a working system, starting with the first pass on what broke, and measure it against plain rules on cost as well as accuracy.
